title: Fring Show 3: The Solve It Squad ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ one of the best parody sh...
transcript: My third fringe show was the absolute hilarious The Solve It squad by the Tin Can Bros. And the solve it squad is essentially a Scooby Doo parody show where a group of former teenage detectives has to get together 20 years later to solve one last mystery. And parody can be tough to nail, but this does a really great job of not only paying homage to the original source material, but also standing on its own. And it can become really easy when doing parody to become essentially predictable. We know the tropes, we know the where this is gonna end up, and this show does a really great job of also keeping the audience surprised. And the solve it squad is incredibly funny. Not just the performances and the writing, but also the direction. There were a lot of really inventive, creative staging choices that I appreciated, which can be really fun to lean on, especially when you're directing on a intense budget like you do at fringe. And there is so much good comedy work in this production, especially from the actors. A lot of great character work, a lot of great object work, some fantastic miming. But I have to shout out Brian Rosenfalk's performance, because he essentially plays the entire ensemble of characters outside of the main four, and he is, like, entire scenes essentially with himself. And to be able to pull off that kind of timing and have it still be really Funny is incredibly hard to do, and he just absolutely nails it. Now, I did see this rather early in its run at fringe, and there were some moments where the music overpowered the voices on stage, and so I hope that they have gotten that fixed since then. But hiccups like that at fringe are to be expected. Overall, I thought this was an incredibly fun and entertaining piece of theater. And if you like parodies and if you like Scooby Doo, this is an absolute must see. And the best part about the solve it squad is that you do not have to be in Edinburgh to watch this one. They do have a digital ticket out option available on their website. They have tickets for both a live stream so you can watch that performance live when it happens, or they do have a video on demand option available. We love accessible streaming options. Definitely check this one out if you get a chance. This is one of my favorite parody shows of the entire fringe. Just absolute stellar work all around.
